## 2. Story question

How can a packet of seeds become a bridge between careful testing and the hope of planting?

## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_41_botanist_the_seeds",
  "text": "The seeds. The Cartographer gave the bunker 10 varieties of heirloom seeds. I opened the packet in the greenhouse at 06:00 and I held them in my hand and I counted them. 10 varieties. Wheat (2 varieties — the Cartographer does not know the names, only that they are wheat), barley, rye, oats, peas, beans, lentils, radish, and a leafy green I do not recognise. The seeds are the Cartographer's cache stock. The seeds have been in the packet for an unknown time. I will test viability with the germination test — 10 seeds of each variety on wet paper, 7 days, count the sprouts. If the germination is above 50 percent, the seeds are plantable. The Cartographer said plant the seeds. The Cartographer said the seeds need a place and the bunker is the place. The seeds are the spring. The spring is the thing that moves the food from the greenhouse to the surface. The greenhouse is the bridge. The surface is the destination. The seeds are the thing that crosses the bridge. I held the seeds in my hand and I thought of Tomas. Tomas would have calculated the probability. I did not calculate. I held. The holding is the thing the Surgeon does with the 304. The holding is the thing I do with the seeds. The 304 are the holding that is a reserve. The seeds are the holding that is a future. The future is the thing that grows. The growing is the thing that happens when the ground remembers. The ground is remembering. The seeds are the thing I will plant when the ground says yes. The ground will say yes by Day 250. The seeds are ready. I am ready. The greenhouse is the bridge. The surface is the destination. The seeds are the crossing.",
  "timestamp": "Day 221, 07h",
  "author_name": "The Botanist",
  "author_id": "the_botanist",
  "knowledge_key": "botanist_cartographer_seeds_10_varieties",
  "day": 221,

Day 250 is the Botanist's expectation, not a confirmed outcome. Do not invent test results, yields, or a surface planting. Eight exact text excerpts recur below as anchors. Read them as source quotations; the plan adds no event beyond the row.

## 14. Re-reading and variation

Use the passage bank as a set of alternatives. A single approved passage should be edited to fit its source voice and surrounding game text; do not stack all options into one entry. Keep the eight source focuses distinct, vary cadence rather than canon, and retain the original timestamp and knowledge key.

## 15. Cross-content fit

The row belongs to the canonical journal corpus. Adjacent references named by the source may guide a later continuity review, but this plan adds no cross-links, unlock order, or new narrative state. Preserve stated measurements, counts, identities, and chronology exactly until an owner reviews any discrepancy.

## 16. Failure and refusal

Reject any candidate that invents an outcome, motive, conversation, test result, settlement reaction, harvest, treatment effect, or future weather state absent from the row. Reject prose that turns an open question into a puzzle, a person into a lesson, or the source's metaphor into a gameplay rule.

## 17. Replay and callback boundary

All proposed writing is static editorial copy. It requires no random selection, replay state, callback key, persistent memory, or new journal deduplication rule. The source row remains governed by its current catalog and knowledge key.

## 18. Implementation classification

**Classification:** narrative/content proposal only; no code, authored JSON, UI route, save section, feature flag, or runtime integration is included. The local corpus confirms the row and its loader authority, not that this expansion is implemented.
